chosen.premise: Magnemite’s side magnets can pull iron objects from more than 300 feet away.
chosen.hook: Magnemite can steal iron from over 300 feet away.
chosen.visualIdea: Place Magnemite at one end of a street and show distant iron objects flying toward its side units.
chosen.note: The 300-foot distance is exceptionally specific and surprising. “Steal” slightly overstates the source, which says Magnemite draws in iron objects.

candidates.premise: Magnemite’s electromagnetic waves cancel gravity, but it falls when its internal electricity runs out.
candidates.hook: Magnemite can defeat gravity—until its battery dies.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Magnemite hovering, its energy meter draining, then dropping to the ground before a battery revives it.
candidates.note: A Pokémon that levitates only while powered is a strong, concrete contradiction, and the battery-draining visual is very clear.

candidates.premise: The faster Magnemite’s side units rotate, the greater the magnetic force they generate.
candidates.hook: For Magnemite, spinning faster means becoming a stronger magnet.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate the side units accelerating as nearby metal objects begin moving toward Magnemite.
candidates.note: A precise mechanical rule directly supported by the Pokédex, though the payoff is less inherently dramatic than the 300-foot range or battery failure.

candidates.premise: Magnemite is attracted to electromagnetic waves and may approach trainers using a Pokégear.
candidates.hook: Your Pokégear could accidentally call a Magnemite over.
candidates.visualIdea: A trainer activates a Pokégear, electromagnetic wave rings spread outward, and Magnemite follows them in.
candidates.note: A charmingly specific interaction with a Pokégear, but it relies on one older entry and has a smaller dramatic payoff.

candidates.premise: Magnemite feeds on electricity and can gather around power lines, breaker boxes, and power plants.
candidates.hook: That power outage might be a Magnemite feeding frenzy.
candidates.visualIdea: Follow a blackout clue from a dark house to breaker boxes, power lines, and a swarm of Magnemite.
candidates.note: Well supported and highly visual, but the broader blackout mystery is less distinctive than Magnemite’s measurable magnet range or flight limitation.

candidates.premise: Magnemite reaches Magneton at level 30, but its final evolution requires leveling up at Mt. Coronet.
candidates.hook: Magnemite’s final evolution depends on where it levels up.
candidates.visualIdea: Compare a level-30 Magnemite evolution with Magneton’s separate final-evolution route at Mt. Coronet.
candidates.note: The location-based evolution is surprising, but the hook is imprecise: Magnemite evolves into Magneton at level 30, while Magneton requires Mt. Coronet for the final evolution.
